### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Journal-specific AI policy page not found for JGP (tandfonline.com blocked fetch with 403); relying on Taylor & Francis's group-wide policy, which applies to all T&F/Routledge journals including this one. Under that policy: generative AI tools cannot be listed as authors; authors remain fully accountable for content originality/validity; use of generative AI must be disclosed (tool name, version, purpose) in the Methods or Acknowledgments section; permitted uses include idea generation, language/grammar polishing, literature search/classification, and coding assistance; prohibited uses include generating or manipulating research data, images, figures, or visuals. T&F notes some individual journals may restrict AI use to language-improvement only, but no such journal-specific restriction for JGP was locatable this session -- leniency is an inferred midpoint (3/5: disclosure-gated, not a ban, not fully open) rather than a confirmed journal-specific figure. |
| **Source URL** | https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/ |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Empirical/experimental psychology papers (basic and applied) with broad appeal to general psychological-science readers, plus quantitative meta-analyses; recent 2024-2025 issues (vol.152) include an online-post content-analysis study on internet anxiety, a face-perception/affective-realism experiment, a judgments-of-learning/memory experiment, and a three-level meta-analysis on trait mindfulness and procrastination.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** controlled/experimental studies (IV manipulation), quantitative meta-analysis, content/text analysis of naturalistic online data, model/theory-testing of complex psychological phenomena
